calculus.title: Calculus — derivatives intro
calculus.body: The derivative f′(a) is the limit of [f(a+h)−f(a)]/h as h→0, when that finite limit exists. It is the instantaneous rate of change and the tangent slope. For y=xⁿ with positive integer n, y′=nxⁿ⁻¹; a constant has derivative zero. A stationary point has derivative zero, but need not be a maximum or minimum.

contrast.en: A difference quotient is an average rate over an interval; the derivative is a limit at a point. At a corner such as |x| at 0 it does not exist.
contrast.ru: Разностное отношение — средняя скорость на промежутке; производная — предел в точке. В угловой точке, например у |x| при 0, производной нет.

proofs.title: Mathematical proof
items: Direct proof — A direct proof derives a statement from its hypotheses using definitions and valid logical steps. For a claim “if P, then Q”, assume P and deduce Q for an arbitrary object satisfying the hypotheses.

Proof by contradiction — A proof by contradiction assumes the negation of the desired statement together with the hypotheses, then derives incompatible conclusions. Since the hypotheses and logical rules are retained, the added negation must be false.

Proof by induction — Mathematical induction proves a claim P(n) for every integer n≥n₀. First prove P(n₀). Then, for an arbitrary k≥n₀, assume P(k) and prove P(k+1). These two steps establish all successive cases.

Counterexample — A counterexample is an allowed instance for which a universal claim fails. One such instance disproves “for every x, P(x)”. To refute “if P then Q”, the example must satisfy P while failing Q.

direct.name: Direct proof
direct.rule: A direct proof derives a statement from its hypotheses using definitions and valid logical steps. For a claim “if P, then Q”, assume P and deduce Q for an arbitrary object satisfying the hypotheses.
examples: Let a=2m and b=2n for integers m,n. Then a+b=2(m+n), and m+n is an integer, so the sum is even.

For a Euclidean triangle, draw a line through the top vertex parallel to the opposite side. Alternate angles reproduce the two base angles at that vertex; together with its angle they form a straight angle of 180°.
PROVE: a² − b² = (a−b)(a+b). Expand right side: (a−b)(a+b) = a² + ab − ab − b² = a² − b². QED.

contrast.en: Several successful examples do not prove a universal claim. State which assumptions and theorem justify each step.
contrast.ru: Несколько удачных примеров не доказывают всеобщее утверждение. Укажите условия и теоремы, обосновывающие шаги.

contradiction.name: Proof by contradiction
contradiction.rule: A proof by contradiction assumes the negation of the desired statement together with the hypotheses, then derives incompatible conclusions. Since the hypotheses and logical rules are retained, the added negation must be false.
examples: PROVE: √2 is irrational. Assume √2 IS rational, so √2 = a/b in lowest terms. Square: 2 = a²/b². So a² = 2b². a² is even → a is even → a = 2k. Then 4k² = 2b² → b² = 2k² → b also even. But a/b was in lowest terms — CONTRADICTION. So √2 is irrational.

PROVE: there are infinitely many primes. Assume finitely many: p₁, p₂, …, pₙ. Consider N = p₁·p₂·…·pₙ + 1. N is not divisible by any pᵢ (remainder 1). So either N is prime (contradicts list being complete) or has a new prime factor.

contrast.en: Negation must be precise: the negation of “all” is “there exists a counterexample”, not “none”.
contrast.ru: Отрицание должно быть точным: отрицание «для всех» — «существует контрпример», а не «ни для одного».

sources.title: Oscar Levin — Discrete Mathematics: An Open Introduction

induction.name: Proof by induction
induction.rule: Mathematical induction proves a claim P(n) for every integer n≥n₀. First prove P(n₀). Then, for an arbitrary k≥n₀, assume P(k) and prove P(k+1). These two steps establish all successive cases.
examples: PROVE: 1 + 2 + … + n = n(n+1)/2. Base: n=1, LHS=1, RHS=1·2/2=1. ✓ Inductive: assume true for k. Add (k+1): k(k+1)/2 + (k+1) = (k+1)(k+2)/2. ✓
PROVE: 2ⁿ > n for all positive integers. Base: 2¹=2>1. ✓ Inductive: 2^(k+1) = 2·2ᵏ > 2k ≥ k+1 (since k ≥ 1). ✓
Divisibility example: PROVE 7ⁿ − 1 is divisible by 6. Base: 7¹−1 = 6. ✓ Inductive: 7^(k+1) − 1 = 7·7ᵏ − 1 = 7(7ᵏ − 1) + 6 = 7·6m + 6 = 6(7m+1). ✓

contrast.en: The inductive assumption concerns an arbitrary k, not the conclusion for every n. The starting value need not be 1.
contrast.ru: Предположение индукции относится к произвольному k, а не к уже доказанному результату для всех n. Начальный номер не обязан быть 1.

counterexample.name: Counterexample
counterexample.rule: A counterexample is an allowed instance for which a universal claim fails. One such instance disproves “for every x, P(x)”. To refute “if P then Q”, the example must satisfy P while failing Q.
examples: CLAIM: 'all primes are odd'. Counterexample: 2 is prime AND even. Disproved.
CLAIM: 'n² > n for all positive integers'. Counterexample: n=1 gives 1²=1, NOT > 1. Disproved.
CLAIM: 'every quadratic has real roots'. Counterexample: x² + 1 = 0 has no real roots. Disproved.
CLAIM: 'if a²=b² then a=b'. Counterexample: a=−3, b=3. Both square to 9 but aren't equal.

contrast.en: A value outside the stated domain is not a counterexample. Passing many checks can support a conjecture but does not prove it for all cases.
contrast.ru: Значение вне указанной области не является контрпримером. Много удачных проверок поддерживает гипотезу, но не доказывает её для всех случаев.

numberTheory.title: Number theory basics
numberTheory.body: A prime is an integer greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors: 1 and itself. Every integer greater than 1 is a product of primes, unique apart from their order. Congruence a≡b (mod m), for positive integer m, means m divides a−b; for example 17≡2 (mod 5).

review.russianTerm: Простое число; разложение на простые множители; сравнение по модулю

contrast.en: 1 is neither prime nor composite. Congruence means equal remainders, not equal numbers.
contrast.ru: 1 не является ни простым, ни составным. Сравнение по модулю означает одинаковые остатки, а не равенство чисел.

complex.title: Complex numbers — preview
complex.body: A complex number has form z=a+bi, where a,b are real and i²=−1. Its real part is a and imaginary part is b. The real numbers form the case b=0. In the complex numbers, x²+1=0 has solutions ±i; real square-root product rules must not be applied blindly to negative radicands.

contrast.en: The imaginary part of 2+3i is 3, not 3i. “Imaginary” is a mathematical name and does not mean invalid.
contrast.ru: Мнимая часть 2+3i равна 3, а не 3i. «Мнимая» — математическое название, а не указание на недопустимость числа.

statsExt.title: Statistics extension
statsExt.body: Population variance is the mean squared deviation from the population mean; standard deviation is its square root. The usual sample variance estimator divides the sum of squared deviations from the sample mean by n−1. Pearson correlation r describes the direction and strength of linear association between paired numerical variables and lies from −1 to 1 when both have nonzero variance.

contrast.en: Zero correlation does not rule out a nonlinear relationship. Correlation alone does not establish causation.
contrast.ru: Нулевая корреляция не исключает нелинейную связь. Одна корреляция не устанавливает причинность.

numberSystems.intro: Classification of numbers, set notation, rounding, surds, exponents, standard form and absolute values.

structureSets.name: Structure & Sets — classification, set notation
structureSets.rule: Natural numbers count: ℕ={1,2,3,…} here. Integers ℤ also include zero and negative whole numbers. Rational numbers ℚ are a/b with integers a,b and b≠0. Real numbers ℝ comprise rational and irrational numbers. Thus ℕ⊂ℤ⊂ℚ⊂ℝ. A∪B contains elements in either set; A∩B contains elements in both; ∅ is empty; x∈A means membership; A⊆B means every element of A is in B.
examples: √2 ∈ ℝ but √2 ∉ ℚ (it's irrational).
0.333… = 1/3 ∈ ℚ (recurring decimals are rational).

contrast.en: An element and a subset are different: 2∈ℕ but {2}⊆ℕ. Some books include 0 in ℕ; state the convention.
contrast.ru: Элемент и подмножество различаются: 2∈ℕ, но {2}⊆ℕ. В некоторых учебниках 0 включают в ℕ; соглашение нужно указывать.

rounding.name: Rounding & accuracy
rounding.rule: Rounding replaces a number by a nearby multiple of a chosen place value. Decimal places count digits after the decimal point; significant figures count from the first nonzero digit. For positive values here, a next digit 5–9 increases the retained digit; 0–4 leaves it unchanged.
examples: 0.004532 ≈ 0.005 (1 s.f.); the first significant digit is 4 and the next is 5.

contrast.en: Precision of the written result differs from accuracy relative to a true value. 1.25×10³ explicitly has three significant figures.
contrast.ru: Точность записи отличается от близости к истинному значению. Запись 1.25×10³ явно содержит три значащие цифры.

model.en: Exact halfway cases depend on the rounding convention. These examples round positive ties upward.
model.ru: Ровно половинные случаи зависят от соглашения. В этих примерах положительные половинные значения округляются вверх.

bounds.name: Upper and lower bounds (Extended)
bounds.rule: If a positive value is rounded to x to the nearest unit d using half-up rounding, its original value v satisfies x−d/2≤v<x+d/2. These endpoints are the lower and upper bounds; the interval describes rounding uncertainty.
examples: Length = 27 cm (nearest cm). LB = 26.5; UB = 27.5.
For positive distance d and time t, average speed v = d/t has lower bound d_L/t_U and upper bound d_U/t_L. A strict endpoint gives a limiting bound, not an attained minimum or maximum.

contrast.en: An upper bound need not be an attainable maximum. Endpoint inclusion changes with the tie rule; bounds do not account for every measurement error.
contrast.ru: Верхняя граница не обязательно достигается. Включение концов зависит от правила округления; границы не учитывают все погрешности измерения.

model.en: For positive distance s and time t, bounds for s/t use s_low/t_high and s_high/t_low, with t_low>0.
model.ru: Для положительных пути s и времени t границы s/t находят как s_low/t_high и s_high/t_low при t_low>0.

exponents.name: Laws of exponents
exponents.rule: For positive integer n, aⁿ is a product of n factors equal to a. Integer exponent laws: aᵐaⁿ=aᵐ⁺ⁿ, aᵐ/aⁿ=aᵐ⁻ⁿ, (aᵐ)ⁿ=aᵐⁿ and (ab)ⁿ=aⁿbⁿ. For a≠0, a⁰=1 and a⁻ⁿ=1/aⁿ. Every denominator must be nonzero.
examples: (2x³)² = 4x⁶.

contrast.en: Adding exponents requires the same base; distributing a power over a product requires the same exponent. A negative exponent means a reciprocal.
contrast.ru: Сложение показателей требует одинакового основания; степень произведения распределяют с одним показателем. Отрицательный показатель означает обратную величину.

fractionalIndices.name: Fractional indices (Extended)
fractionalIndices.rule: For a>0 and integers m,n with n>0, a^(m/n)=(ⁿ√a)ᵐ. The positive nth root is the number whose nth power is a. A negative exponent additionally takes the reciprocal.

contrast.en: √a denotes the nonnegative square root, whereas solving x²=a may give two solutions. For negative a, real roots and exponent laws require separate domain checks.
contrast.ru: √a обозначает неотрицательный квадратный корень, а уравнение x²=a может иметь два корня. Для a<0 действительные корни и свойства степеней требуют отдельной проверки области определения.

model.en: The main exponent rule here uses a>0. Even real roots require nonnegative radicands; odd roots such as ∛(−8)=−2 exist.
model.ru: Основное правило здесь дано при a>0. Для действительного корня чётной степени подкоренное выражение неотрицательно; нечётные корни, например ∛(−8)=−2, существуют.

standardForm.name: Standard form (scientific notation)
standardForm.rule: Scientific notation writes a nonzero real number as a×10ⁿ, where n is an integer and 1≤|a|<10. For positive numbers this is 1≤a<10. The coefficient holds the significant digits; n gives the power of ten. Zero is written separately as 0.
examples: Speed of light: 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

contrast.en: 5.4×10⁵=54×10⁴ numerically, but only the first is normalised scientific notation. Standard form has other meanings for polynomials.
contrast.ru: Численно 5.4×10⁵=54×10⁴, но только первая запись нормализована. Английское standard form имеет и другие значения для многочленов.

unitConversion.name: Conversion of units
unitConversion.rule: Unit conversion expresses the same quantity with another unit. Multiply by a ratio equal to one: 1 km=1000 m, 1 t=1000 kg, 1 L=1000 cm³ and 1 m³=1000 L. Square length conversion factors for area, cube them for volume, and convert numerator and denominator for compound units.
examples: 5 m² = 5 × 100 × 100 = 50,000 cm² (because 1 m² has 100×100 cm²).

contrast.en: A numerical value changes when the unit changes; the physical quantity stays the same. 1 m²=10,000 cm², not 100 cm².
contrast.ru: При смене единицы меняется числовое значение, но сама величина сохраняется. 1 м²=10 000 см², а не 100 см².

surdsSimplify.name: Surds — simplifying
surdsSimplify.rule: A surd is an irrational root of a rational number, kept in exact root form. Here we mainly use √n for positive integers n that are not perfect squares. Simplify by taking square factors out: √(a²b)=|a|√b for real a and b≥0.
examples: √(8x²)=2|x|√2 for real x; when x=−1, the result is 2√2.

contrast.en: A radical is the root notation; a surd has an irrational value. √9=3 is a radical expression but not a surd. π is irrational but is not a surd.
contrast.ru: Радикал — знак корня; surd имеет иррациональное значение. √9=3 записано с радикалом, но это не surd. Число π иррационально, но не является surd.

surdsOperate.name: Surds — operations & rationalising
surdsOperate.rule: Simplify radicals before combining like terms: p√d+q√d=(p+q)√d. For a,b≥0, √a√b=√(ab); for b>0, √a/√b=√(a/b). Rationalising rewrites a fraction with a rational denominator by multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor, often a conjugate.
examples: (2+√5)(2−√5) = 4 − 5 = −1 (difference of squares).

contrast.en: A conjugate changes the middle sign: 3+√2 and 3−√2. Roots do not distribute over addition: √(a+b) is generally not √a+√b.
contrast.ru: Сопряжённые выражения отличаются знаком между слагаемыми: 3+√2 и 3−√2. Корень в общем случае не распределяется по сумме: √(a+b)≠√a+√b.

absolute.name: Absolute values
absolute.rule: For a real number x, |x| is its distance from zero on the number line: |x|=x for x≥0 and |x|=−x for x<0. Thus |x|≥0 and |a−b| is the distance between a and b.
examples: |x − 5| = 3 means x = 8 or x = 2.

contrast.en: An absolute value is a nonnegative magnitude, not a rule that always changes the sign. For k>0, |x|<k means −k<x<k; |x|>k means x<−k or x>k.
contrast.ru: Модуль — неотрицательная величина, а не правило обязательной смены знака. При k>0 условие |x|<k равносильно −k<x<k; |x|>k — условию x<−k или x>k.

functionsAlgebra.title: Functions & Algebra
functionsAlgebra.intro: This page covers mappings, domain and range, quadratic expressions, quadratic functions and their graphs, and transformations of graphs. Then come solving quadratic equations, rearranging formulae, algebraic fractions, proportion, asymptotes and exponential functions.

mappings.name: Mappings, domain and range
mappings.rule: A mapping pairs each element of one set with an element of another set. A function is a mapping in which each input has exactly one output. The domain is the set of input values; the range is the set of output values the function actually produces.
examples: f(x) = x², domain ℝ, range [0, ∞).
g(x) = 1/x, domain ℝ \ {0}, range ℝ \ {0}.
h(x) = √x, domain [0, ∞), range [0, ∞).
If f(x) = 3x − 2, then f(4) = 10 and f(−1) = −5.

contrast.en: Two different inputs can give the same output: y = x² gives 4 for both x = 2 and x = −2. One input can never give two different outputs. Do not mix up the domain (the allowed inputs) with the range (the outputs that actually occur). Exam tip: when you are asked for the range, write outputs, not inputs.
contrast.ru: Два разных аргумента могут дать одно и то же значение: y = x² равно 4 при x = 2 и при x = −2. Один аргумент не может дать два разных значения. Не путай область определения (допустимые аргументы) и область значений (значения, которые функция действительно даёт). Если на экзамене спрашивают область значений, пиши значения функции, а не аргументы.

sources.title: Фоксфорд Учебник — Понятие функции и способы её задания

caption.en: Put −2, 0 and 2 into the rule. The outputs are 4, 0 and 4, so the range for these inputs is {0, 4}.
caption.ru: Подставь −2, 0 и 2 в правило. Получаются значения 4, 0 и 4, значит, область значений для этих аргументов — {0, 4}.

verticalLine.name: Vertical line test: when a graph is a function
verticalLine.rule: A graph shows y as a function of x if every vertical line crosses it at most once. If a vertical line crosses the graph two or more times, one x-value gives two or more y-values, so the graph is not a function.
examples: y = x² is a function: every vertical line crosses its parabola at most once.
x = y² is not a function: the vertical line x = 1 meets the graph at y = 1 and y = −1.
The circle x² + y² = 4 is not a function. The vertical line x = 0 crosses it at y = 2 and at y = −2.

contrast.en: Do not confuse many-to-one with one-to-many. Several x-values can share one y-value, as in y = x²: x = √5 and x = −√5 (≈ ±2.24) both give y = 5, and this is allowed. One x-value giving two y-values is not allowed, as in y² = x: x = 4 gives y = 2 and y = −2.
contrast.ru: Не путай два случая: несколько значений x могут давать одно значение y, а один x — два значения y. В y = x² при x = √5 и x = −√5 (≈ ±2,24) получаем y = 5, и это допустимо для функции. В y² = x один x даёт два значения y: при x = 4 получаем y = 2 и y = −2, и это уже не функция.

sources.title: Фоксфорд Учебник — Понятие функции и способы её задания

quadraticsFactor.name: Expanding and factorising quadratic expressions
quadraticsFactor.rule: A quadratic expression has the form ax² + bx + c, where a ≠ 0. Expanding removes brackets: multiply every term in one bracket by every term in the other. Factorising does the reverse: it writes the expression as brackets multiplied together. Do not mix up the two words: terms are added (x², 7x, 12), but factors are multiplied, as in (x + 3)(x + 4).
examples: Expand: (x + 3)(x − 5) = x² − 2x − 15.
Factorise: x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4), because 3 × 4 = 12 and 3 + 4 = 7.
Factorise: x² − 5x − 14 = (x − 7)(x + 2), because −7 × 2 = −14 and −7 + 2 = −5.
Difference of squares: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3).
Leading coefficient 2: 2x² + 7x + 3 = (2x + 1)(x + 3). Check the middle term: 2 × 3 + 1 × 1 = 7, and the constant term: 1 × 3 = 3.

contrast.en: Do not confuse factorising with solving. (x + 3)(x + 4) is an expression, but (x + 3)(x + 4) = 0 is an equation. For x² + bx + c = (x + p)(x + q), you need p + q = b and pq = c. Some quadratic expressions cannot be factorised using whole numbers.
contrast.ru: Не путай разложение с решением. (x + 3)(x + 4) — это выражение, а (x + 3)(x + 4) = 0 — уравнение. Для x² + bx + c = (x + p)(x + q) нужно, чтобы p + q = b и pq = c. Некоторые квадратные выражения нельзя разложить на множители с целыми числами.

caption.en: The first two expressions are equal for every x. Setting (x + 3)(x + 4) equal to 0 gives an equation with two solutions.

quadraticsGraph.name: Quadratic graphs: the parabola, its intercepts and its vertex
quadraticsGraph.rule: A quadratic function f(x) = ax² + bx + c, where a ≠ 0, has a parabola as its graph. The parabola crosses the y-axis at (0, c). Its x-intercepts are the points where f(x) = 0. The vertex is the lowest point if a > 0, and the highest point if a < 0. Its x-coordinate is −b/(2a).
examples: y = x² − 4x + 3 opens upwards. It crosses the y-axis at (0, 3) and the x-axis at x = 1 and x = 3.
y = −x² + 4 opens downwards. It crosses the y-axis at (0, 4) and the x-axis at x = −2 and x = 2.
For y = −x² + 2x + 3, x = −b/(2a) = −2/(2 × (−1)) = 1. Then y = −1 + 2 + 3 = 4, so the vertex is (1, 4). It is a maximum, because a = −1 is negative.

contrast.en: Do not confuse a root with an intercept. A root is an x-value, for example x = 2. An x-intercept is a point, for example (2, 0). A double root means the parabola touches the x-axis at its vertex without crossing it.
contrast.ru: Не путай корень и точку пересечения. Корень — это значение x, например x = 2. Точка пересечения с осью x — это точка (2; 0). Двойной корень означает, что парабола касается оси x в вершине и не пересекает её.

vertexForm.name: Vertex form: the vertex, the axis of symmetry and completing the square
vertexForm.rule: The vertex form is y = a(x − h)² + k, where a ≠ 0. The vertex is the point (h, k), and the axis of symmetry is the line x = h. The value k is the minimum of y if a > 0, and the maximum if a < 0. Completing the square changes ax² + bx + c into this form without changing its values.
examples: Complete the square: x² − 6x + 5 = (x − 3)² − 4, so the vertex is (3, −4).
For y = 2x² + 8x − 3, take 2 out of the first two terms: y = 2(x² + 4x) − 3. Complete the square inside the bracket: y = 2[(x + 2)² − 4] − 3 = 2(x + 2)² − 11. So the vertex is (−2, −11).

contrast.en: Watch the sign. In (x + 2)², the value of h is −2, because the bracket is (x − h). If a ≠ 1, take a out of the x² and x terms first, and leave the constant term outside the bracket.
contrast.ru: Смотри на знак. В (x + 2)² значение h равно −2, потому что в скобке стоит x − h. Если a ≠ 1, сначала вынеси a только из членов с x² и x, а свободный член оставь за скобками.

transformations.name: Transformations of graphs: shifts, stretches and reflections
transformations.rule:
A transformation changes the position or the shape of a graph. In y = a f(x − h) + k, h shifts the graph right by h units, and k shifts it up by k units. If h or k is negative, the shift goes the opposite way. The value |a| is the vertical stretch factor, and a negative a also reflects the graph in the x-axis.

Extended: for y = f(bx), the graph is stretched horizontally by the factor 1/|b|, and a negative b reflects it in the y-axis.
examples: y = (x − 3)² + 2 is the graph of y = x² moved 3 units right and 2 units up. Its vertex is (3, 2).
y = 2x² is the graph of y = x² stretched vertically by factor 2: every y-value doubles. For example, when x = 1, y changes from 1 to 2.

Extended: y = (2x)² = 4x². For y = x², a horizontal scale factor of 1/2 gives the same graph as a vertical stretch by factor 4. For y = x³, the same horizontal factor gives a vertical stretch by factor 8, so the vertical factor depends on the function.
y = −x² is the graph of y = x² reflected in the x-axis. The point (2, 4) on y = x² moves to (2, −4).

contrast.en: f(2x) compresses the graph horizontally: every horizontal distance is halved, so the horizontal scale factor is 1/2. The order of stretching and shifting matters, because doing them in a different order can give a different graph.
contrast.ru: f(2x) сжимает график по горизонтали: все горизонтальные расстояния уменьшаются вдвое, поэтому коэффициент растяжения по горизонтали равен 1/2. Порядок растяжения и сдвига важен: в другом порядке эти действия могут дать другой график.

solveGeneral.name: Quadratic equations and their real roots
solveGeneral.rule: An equation is a statement that two expressions are equal. A solution is a value of the variable that makes the equation true. A quadratic equation can be written as ax² + bx + c = 0, where a ≠ 0. The discriminant, Δ = b² − 4ac, shows how many real roots there are: two distinct roots if Δ > 0, one repeated root if Δ = 0, and no real roots if Δ < 0.
examples: x² − 4x + 4 = 0: Δ = (−4)² − 4 × 1 × 4 = 0, so there is one repeated root, x = 2.
x² + x + 1 = 0: Δ = 1² − 4 × 1 × 1 = −3 < 0, so there are no real solutions.

contrast.en: You simplify or factorise an expression, but you solve an equation to find the values of x.
contrast.ru: Выражение упрощают или раскладывают на множители, а уравнение решают, чтобы найти значения x.

solveFactor.name: Solving quadratic equations by factorising
solveFactor.rule: If two numbers multiply to give zero, at least one of them is zero. First move all the terms to one side, so that the other side is zero, then factorise the expression. Then set each bracket equal to zero and solve: if (x − p)(x − q) = 0, then x = p or x = q.
examples: x² + 2x = 0: take out the common factor x to get x(x + 2) = 0, so x = 0 or x = −2.
x² = 16: subtract 16 to get x² − 16 = 0, so (x − 4)(x + 4) = 0 and x = 4 or x = −4.

contrast.en: This rule works only when the brackets multiply to give zero: in (x − 2)(x − 3) = 5, you cannot set each bracket equal to 5. Dividing both sides of x² = 3x by x loses the solution x = 0.
contrast.ru: Это правило работает только тогда, когда произведение равно нулю: в (x − 2)(x − 3) = 5 нельзя приравнять каждую скобку к 5. Деление обеих частей x² = 3x на x теряет решение x = 0.

solveCompleteSquare.name: Solving quadratic equations by completing the square
solveCompleteSquare.rule: Completing the square rewrites x² + 2px as (x + p)² − p². Isolate the squared bracket to get (x + p)² = q. If q ≥ 0, the solutions are x = −p ± √q; if q < 0, there are no real solutions. When the equation has the form ax² + bx + c = 0, first divide every term by a, where a ≠ 0.
examples: x² + 6x − 7 = 0: (x + 3)² − 9 − 7 = 0, so (x + 3)² = 16 and x + 3 = ±4. Therefore x = 1 or x = −7.

contrast.en: The symbol √q gives only the non-negative root, so the ± sign is needed. For example, both 4 and −4 square to 16.
contrast.ru: Символ √q обозначает только неотрицательный корень, поэтому нужен знак ±. Например, и 4, и −4 при возведении в квадрат дают 16.

solveFormula.name: Solving quadratic equations with the quadratic formula
solveFormula.rule: For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, with a ≠ 0, the quadratic formula gives the solutions x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a). The part under the square root, Δ = b² − 4ac, is the discriminant. If Δ ≥ 0, the formula gives real solutions; if Δ < 0, there are no real solutions. Divide the whole numerator by 2a, and take care with signs: if b = −5, then −b = 5.

contrast.en: An exact answer can contain a square root, such as (5 ± √17) / 4. Write a decimal approximation with ≈ and round only the final answer.
contrast.ru: Точный ответ может содержать квадратный корень, например (5 ± √17) / 4. Приближённое значение пиши со знаком ≈ и округляй только итоговый ответ.

solveGraphical.name: Solving equations graphically
solveGraphical.rule: A solution of f(x) = 0 is an x-value where the graph of y = f(x) crosses or touches the x-axis. A solution of f(x) = g(x) is an x-value where the graphs of y = f(x) and y = g(x) meet. If the graph only touches the x-axis, that point is still a solution, called a repeated root.
examples: To solve x² − 4 = 0, plot y = x² − 4. It crosses the x-axis at x = −2 and x = 2.
To solve x² = x + 2, plot y = x² and y = x + 2. The graphs meet at two points, where x = −1 and x = 2, so these are the solutions.

contrast.en: A graph gives an estimate, not an exact answer. Check your answer by substituting it into the equation. A viewing window that is too small can hide a solution.
contrast.ru: График даёт приближённый ответ, а не точный. Проверь ответ, подставив его в уравнение. Слишком маленькое окно графика может скрыть решение.

sources.title: Фоксфорд Учебник — Понятие функции и способы её задания

rearrange.name: Rearranging a formula to make a chosen variable the subject
rearrange.rule: A formula is an equation that shows how quantities are related. Changing the subject means rearranging the formula so that one chosen variable is on its own on one side. Do the same operation to both sides, and check that you never divide by zero. After you take a square root, choose the sign using the context of the problem.
examples: Make r the subject of A = πr²: r² = A/π, so r = √(A/π). A radius is positive, so take the positive root. For A = 50 cm², r ≈ 3.99 cm.
Make t the subject of v = u + at. Subtract u from both sides: v − u = at. Divide both sides by a (a ≠ 0): t = (v − u)/a. Check with v = 20 m/s, u = 5 m/s and a = 3 m/s²: t = (20 − 5)/3 = 5 s.
Make h the subject of V = πr²h/3. Multiply both sides by 3: 3V = πr²h. Divide by πr² (r ≠ 0): h = 3V/(πr²). Check with r = 2 cm and V = 8π cm³: h = 3 × 8π/(π × 2²) = 6 cm.

Make x the subject of y = (x + 1)/(x − 2), where x ≠ 2. Multiply both sides by (x − 2): y(x − 2) = x + 1. Expand: yx − 2y = x + 1. Move the x terms to the left: yx − x = 2y + 1. Take x outside the brackets: x(y − 1) = 2y + 1, so x = (2y + 1)/(y − 1), where y ≠ 1. Check with y = 2: x = 5, and (5 + 1)/(5 − 2) = 2.

contrast.en: A radius cannot be negative, so from A = πr² we get r = √(A/π), not ±√(A/π). From v = u + at, t = (v − u)/a only when a ≠ 0.
contrast.ru: Радиус не может быть отрицательным, поэтому из A = πr² получаем r = √(A/π), а не ±√(A/π). Из v = u + at получаем t = (v − u)/a только при a ≠ 0.

algebraicFractions.name: Simplifying algebraic fractions; Extended: solving equations with them
algebraicFractions.rule:
An algebraic fraction (rational algebraic expression) is one algebraic expression divided by another. It is undefined when its denominator is zero, so state the values that are not allowed, for example x ≠ 0. Add fractions over a common denominator, multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators, and divide by multiplying by the reciprocal. Factorise first, then cancel common factors; cancelling does not remove the restrictions on the variable.

Extended: when you multiply both sides of an equation by an expression that contains the variable, check every solution in the original equation.
examples: Solve 3/(x − 1) + 2/(x + 1) = 1, where x ≠ 1 and x ≠ −1. Multiply both sides by (x − 1)(x + 1): 3(x + 1) + 2(x − 1) = (x − 1)(x + 1). This gives 5x + 1 = x² − 1, so x² − 5x − 2 = 0. Then x = (5 ± √33)/2, so x ≈ 5.37 or x ≈ −0.37. Both values are allowed.

contrast.en: Cancel common factors, not terms. (x² − 4)/(x − 2) = x + 2 for x ≠ 2, but in (x + 1)/x the x cannot be cancelled, because x is not a factor of the whole numerator (x + 1).
contrast.ru: Сокращай общие множители, а не слагаемые. (x² − 4)/(x − 2) = x + 2 при x ≠ 2, но в (x + 1)/x сокращать x нельзя: это не множитель всего числителя (x + 1).

proportions.name: Direct and inverse proportion: y = kx and y = k/x
proportions.rule: Two quantities are directly proportional if y = kx, where k is a non-zero constant called the constant of proportionality. Then y/x = k for every x ≠ 0, and the graph is a straight line through the origin. Two quantities are inversely proportional if y = k/x, so xy = k. Doubling x halves y. To find k, substitute one known pair of values. If y is proportional to x², then y = kx².
examples: Cost is directly proportional to weight. If 3 kg cost £6, then k = 6 ÷ 3 = £2 per kg. So 5 kg cost 2 × 5 = £10.
Time is inversely proportional to speed for a fixed distance. At 60 km/h a trip takes 4 hours, so the distance is k = 60 × 4 = 240 km. At 80 km/h the time is 240 ÷ 80 = 3 hours.

The area of a circle is directly proportional to the square of its radius: A = πr², so k = π. With r = 2 cm, A = 4π ≈ 12.6 cm². With r = 4 cm, A = 16π ≈ 50.3 cm². Doubling the radius makes the area four times bigger.
4 people finish a job in 6 days, so k = 4 × 6 = 24 person-days. With 8 people, the job takes 24 ÷ 8 = 3 days.

contrast.en: The line y = mx + c with c ≠ 0 is not direct proportion, because it does not pass through the origin. A decreasing graph is not automatically inverse proportion: y must equal k/x.
contrast.ru: График y = mx + c при c ≠ 0 — это не прямая пропорциональность: он не проходит через начало координат. Убывающий график ещё не означает обратную пропорциональность: y должен равняться k/x.

model.en: Real situations need fixed conditions. Time and speed are inversely proportional only when the distance stays the same.
model.ru: Реальные ситуации требуют постоянных условий. Время и скорость обратно пропорциональны только при одинаковом расстоянии.

asymptotes.name: Extended: asymptotes of rational functions
asymptotes.rule: An asymptote is a line that a graph gets closer and closer to. A vertical asymptote is at x = c, where the denominator is zero and the factor does not cancel. A horizontal asymptote y = L shows the value the function approaches as |x| becomes very large. For f(x) = a/(x − h) + k, with a ≠ 0, the asymptotes are x = h and y = k.
examples: y = 1/(x − 3): the vertical asymptote is x = 3, because the denominator is zero there. The horizontal asymptote is y = 0. For example, y = 1 when x = 4.
y = (x + 1)/(x − 2) = 1 + 3/(x − 2). The vertical asymptote is x = 2, and the horizontal asymptote is y = 1. Check with x = 5: (5 + 1)/(5 − 2) = 2 and 1 + 3/3 = 2.
y = 1/x²: the vertical asymptote is x = 0 and the horizontal asymptote is y = 0. Unlike y = 1/x, the graph stays above the x-axis, because x² is always greater than zero when x ≠ 0.

contrast.en: If a zero of the denominator cancels, the graph has a hole, not an asymptote. For (x² − 4)/(x − 2), the hole is at (2, 4). A graph can cross its horizontal asymptote.
contrast.ru: Если ноль знаменателя сокращается, на графике будет выколотая точка, а не асимптота. У (x² − 4)/(x − 2) выколота точка (2; 4). График может пересекать горизонтальную асимптоту.

exponential.name: Extended: exponential functions — growth and decay
exponential.rule: An exponential function has the form y = A·bˣ, where A is the starting value and b is the constant growth factor (A > 0, b > 0, b ≠ 1). Each time x increases by 1, y is multiplied by b. The graph passes through (0, A). If b > 1, the function shows growth. If 0 < b < 1, it shows decay.
examples: y = 2ˣ: each time x increases by 1, y doubles. Check: y(0) = 1, y(1) = 2 and y(3) = 8.
A laptop is worth £100 and loses 10% of its value each year, so V = 100 × 0.9ᵗ, where t is the number of years. After 1 year V = £90, and after 2 years V = £81.
Compound interest: A = P(1 + r)ⁿ, where P is the starting sum, r is the yearly rate as a decimal and n is the number of years. For £500 at 4% a year for 3 years: A = 500 × 1.04³ ≈ £562.43.

Bacteria: N = N₀ × 2⁽ᵗ/ᵀ⁾, where N₀ is the starting number, t is the time in hours and T is the doubling time. A colony starts with 100 cells and doubles every 3 hours. After 6 hours: N = 100 × 2⁽⁶/³⁾ = 100 × 2² = 400 cells.

contrast.en: In bˣ the variable is the power, so y = 2ˣ doubles at each step. In x² the variable is the base: at x = 1, 2, 3 the values are 1, 4 and 9, and the ratio between steps is not fixed. A fixed percentage change is not the same as a fixed amount added each time.
contrast.ru: В bˣ переменная стоит в показателе, поэтому y = 2ˣ удваивается на каждом шаге. В x² переменная — основание: при x = 1, 2, 3 значения равны 1, 4 и 9, и множитель между шагами не постоянен. Постоянный процентный рост не совпадает с постоянной прибавкой.

model.ru: Постоянный темп роста — это допущение модели. Численность населения и цены не могут расти с одним и тем же темпом неограниченно долго.

sequences.title: Sequences & Series
sequences.intro: Arithmetic sequences: the rule for the nth term and the sum of the first n terms. Extended: geometric sequences: the rule for the nth term, and the sum to infinity of a geometric series.

linearGeneral.name: Arithmetic sequences: recursive and explicit formulas
linearGeneral.rule:
An arithmetic sequence is a sequence in which the difference between consecutive terms is constant. This constant is the common difference, d.

With first term u₁, the recursive formula is uₙ₊₁ = uₙ + d, so each term is the previous term plus d. The explicit formula gives any term directly: uₙ = u₁ + (n − 1)d, where u₁ is the first term and n is the term number, a positive whole number.

The graph of an arithmetic sequence is a set of separate points on a straight line, because n takes only whole-number values.
examples: Using uₙ = 23 − 3n for the sequence 20, 17, 14, …, the 10th term is u₁₀ = 23 − 30 = −7.
What is the 100th term of 7, 12, 17, …? Here u₁ = 7 and d = 5, so u₁₀₀ = 7 + 99 × 5 = 502.

contrast.en: A term is one value: u₄ = 14 in 5, 8, 11, 14. A sum adds several terms: the sum of the first four terms is 5 + 8 + 11 + 14 = 38.
contrast.ru: Член — одно значение: u₄ = 14 в последовательности 5, 8, 11, 14. Сумма — результат сложения нескольких членов: сумма первых четырёх членов равна 5 + 8 + 11 + 14 = 38.

linearProblems.name: Solving problems with arithmetic sequences: u₁, d and the term number
linearProblems.rule:
Two known terms give the common difference. If uₚ and u_q are known, then u_q − uₚ = (q − p)d, so d = (u_q − uₚ) ÷ (q − p) when p ≠ q. Then use uₚ = u₁ + (p − 1)d to find u₁.

To check whether a value occurs in the sequence, solve u₁ + (n − 1)d = value for n. The value occurs only if n is a positive whole number.
examples: The 5th term is 22 and the 10th term is 47. Find u₁ and d. Since u₁₀ − u₅ = 5d, we get 47 − 22 = 5d, so d = 5. Then u₁ = u₅ − 4d = 22 − 4 × 5 = 2.
Is 200 a term of 3, 7, 11, …? Here u₁ = 3 and d = 4. From 200 = 3 + 4(n − 1) we get 4(n − 1) = 197, so n − 1 = 49.25 and n = 50.25. The term number must be a whole number, so 200 is not a term.
Let S₂₀ be the sum of the first 20 terms of 2, 5, 8, …. Use Sₙ = n(u₁ + uₙ) ÷ 2. Here u₁ = 2, d = 3 and u₂₀ = 2 + 19 × 3 = 59, so S₂₀ = 20 × (2 + 59) ÷ 2 = 610.

contrast.en: Do not take the difference between any two terms as d. The difference u₈ − u₃ equals 5d, because there are 5 steps from the 3rd term to the 8th.
contrast.ru: Не принимай разность любых двух членов за d. Разность u₈ − u₃ равна 5d: от 3-го члена до 8-го — 5 шагов.

geometric.name: Extended: geometric sequences: the common ratio and the nth term
geometric.rule:
Extended: a geometric sequence is a sequence in which the ratio between consecutive terms is constant. This constant is the common ratio, r, so each term is r times the previous term.

With first term u₁, the recursive formula is uₙ₊₁ = r uₙ. The explicit formula is uₙ = u₁rⁿ⁻¹, where n is the term number, a positive whole number. The common ratio cannot be 0, and you cannot divide by a term that is 0 when you find r.
examples: $500 invested at 4% per year: 500, 520, 540.8, …, so r = 1.04. After n years the amount is 500 × 1.04ⁿ, where n = 0 is the starting amount.

contrast.en: Compare with the arithmetic case, where the terms change by a fixed amount d. Here they change by a fixed factor r, so check r first. If −1 < r < 1, the terms get closer to 0. If r > 1 or r < −1, their size grows. If r < 0, the signs alternate.
contrast.ru: Сравни с арифметической прогрессией. Там члены меняются на одну и ту же величину d. Здесь они умножаются на один и тот же множитель r, поэтому сначала проверь r. Если −1 < r < 1, члены приближаются к 0. Если r > 1 или r < −1, их модули растут. Если r < 0, знаки чередуются.

sumInfinity.name: Extended: sum to infinity of a geometric series
sumInfinity.rule:
A series is the sum of the terms of a sequence.

Extended: the sum to infinity, S∞, is the value that the sums of the first n terms approach as n grows. If the first term u₁ is not 0, S∞ exists only when −1 < r < 1. Then S∞ = u₁ ÷ (1 − r).
examples: The recurring decimal 0.111… = 0.1 + 0.01 + 0.001 + …, with u₁ = 0.1 and r = 0.1. So S∞ = 0.1 ÷ 0.9 = 1/9.

contrast.en: Do not use the formula when |r| ≥ 1. For 1 − 1 + 1 − 1 + … (r = −1) the formula would give 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5, but the partial sums 1, 0, 1, 0, … do not settle, so there is no sum to infinity. For r = 1 the formula divides by 0.
contrast.ru: Формулу нельзя применять при |r| ≥ 1. Для 1 − 1 + 1 − 1 + … (r = −1) формула дала бы 1 : 2 = 0,5, но частичные суммы 1, 0, 1, 0, … не приближаются к одному числу, значит, бесконечной суммы нет. При r = 1 в формуле получается деление на 0.

geometryTrig.title: Geometry & Trigonometry
geometryTrig.intro: This page covers right-angled triangles, bearings and circles, plus Extended rules for other triangles. Pythagoras and the trigonometric ratios work only in right-angled triangles. Parts marked Extended are higher-level content: the converse of Pythagoras, the sine and cosine rules and the area formula ½ab sin C.

pythagoras.name: Pythagorean theorem
pythagoras.rule:
In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c². Here a and b are the legs, the sides that meet at the right angle. The hypotenuse c is opposite the right angle and is always the longest side.

Extended: the converse is also true. If the sides of a triangle satisfy a² + b² = c², where c is the longest side, then the angle opposite c is 90°.

In the exam, first decide whether you are finding the hypotenuse or a leg. Add the squares of the legs to find the hypotenuse, and subtract the square of the known leg from the square of the hypotenuse to find a leg.
examples: Legs 3 cm and 4 cm: hypotenuse c = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 cm.
Hypotenuse 13 cm and one leg 5 cm: the other leg is b = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 cm.
Extended: is a triangle with sides 7 cm, 24 cm and 25 cm right-angled? 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625 = 25², so yes.
A 5 m ladder stands against a wall with its foot 3 m from the wall. The top of the ladder reaches a height h on the wall: h = √(5² − 3²) = √16 = 4 m.

contrast.en: Pythagoras works only when the triangle has a right angle. If there is no right angle, a² + b² = c² does not work, so use the cosine rule (Extended) instead.
contrast.ru: Теорема Пифагора работает только тогда, когда в треугольнике есть прямой угол. Если прямого угла нет, формула a² + b² = c² не работает, поэтому используй теорему косинусов (Extended).

trig.name: Sine, cosine and tangent of an acute angle
trig.rule:
Take an acute angle θ in a right-angled triangle. The hypotenuse does not depend on which angle you choose. The opposite side is across from θ, and the adjacent side is next to θ. Their names depend on θ. The three ratios are:


sin θ = opposite / hypotenuse

cos θ = adjacent / hypotenuse

tan θ = opposite / adjacent

To find an angle from a ratio, use the inverse functions sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ and tan⁻¹ on your calculator. The memory aid SOH–CAH–TOA lists the three ratios.

On the exam, check that your calculator is in degree mode, and keep unrounded values until the final answer.
examples: Find the angle θ when the hypotenuse is 10 cm and the adjacent side is 6 cm. cos θ = 6 / 10 = 0.6, so θ = cos⁻¹(0.6) ≈ 53.1°.
Find the opposite side when the hypotenuse is 8 cm and θ = 30°. Opposite side = 8 × sin 30° = 8 × 0.5 = 4 cm.
A tower is 50 m tall. You stand 80 m from its base and look at the top. The angle of elevation θ satisfies tan θ = 50 / 80 = 0.625, so θ ≈ 32°.
The angle of depression from a cliff top to a boat equals the angle of elevation from the boat to the top. These are alternate angles, because the two horizontal lines are parallel.

contrast.en: sin⁻¹ means the inverse function (arcsin), not 1 / sin. The ratios apply only to acute angles, 0° < θ < 90°, in a right-angled triangle.
contrast.ru: Запись sin⁻¹ означает обратную функцию (arcsin), а не 1 / sin. Отношения работают только для острых углов, 0° < θ < 90°, в прямоугольном треугольнике.

bearings.name: Three-figure bearings
bearings.rule:
A bearing is an angle, in degrees, measured clockwise from north at the starting point. Write it with three figures from 000° to 359°: east is 090°, south is 180° and west is 270°.

Imagine standing at the starting point and facing north. The bearing is the angle you turn to your right until you face the target. If you walk a distance d on bearing θ, you move d sin θ east and d cos θ north.

In the exam, first draw a diagram with north, the starting point and the target, then check that the angle is measured clockwise from north.
examples: The bearing of B from A is 060°. The back bearing, the bearing of A from B, is 060° + 180° = 240°.
Point Q is 5 km from P on a bearing of 110°. Put P at the origin. Then Δx = 5 sin 110° ≈ 4.70 km and Δy = 5 cos 110° ≈ −1.71 km. So Q is 4.70 km east and 1.71 km south of P.
A forward bearing of 180° has a back bearing of 000°, not 360°, because bearings run from 000° to 359°.

contrast.en: Do not confuse a bearing with the usual maths angle, which is measured from the x-axis anticlockwise. So for a bearing, the sine and cosine swap places: Δx = d sin θ, not d cos θ.
contrast.ru: Не путай азимут с обычным углом в математике: тот отсчитывают от оси x против часовой стрелки. Поэтому у азимута синус и косинус меняются местами: Δx = d sin θ, а не d cos θ.

sineCosine.name: Sine & Cosine rules (Extended)
sineCosine.rule:
In any triangle, label each side with the letter of the opposite angle: side a is opposite angle A, side b is opposite B, and side c is opposite C.


Sine rule: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C

Cosine rule: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A

Use the sine rule when you know a side and the angle opposite it. Use the cosine rule when you know two sides and the angle between them, or all three sides.

Before you choose a rule, check whether you have a matching side and opposite angle, or the angle between two known sides.
examples: In a triangle, two angles are 40° and 60°, and the side opposite 60° is 8 cm. Find the side opposite 40°: x = 8 × sin 40° / sin 60° ≈ 5.94 cm.
The sides 7 cm and 9 cm enclose an angle of 50°. Use the cosine rule: x = √(7² + 9² − 2 × 7 × 9 × cos 50°) ≈ 7.00 cm.
Cosine rule with three sides known: sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm. For the angle A opposite the 5 cm side: cos A = (6² + 7² − 5²) / (2 × 6 × 7) = 60 / 84 ≈ 0.714, so A ≈ 44.4°.

contrast.en: If you know two sides and the angle between them (SAS), you cannot use the sine rule directly; use the cosine rule. With two sides and an angle opposite one of them (SSA), there can be zero, one or two triangles.
contrast.ru: Если даны две стороны и угол между ними (SAS), теорему синусов напрямую применить нельзя: нужна теорема косинусов. Если даны две стороны и угол напротив одной из них (SSA), треугольников может быть ноль, один или два.

triangleArea.name: Area from two sides and the angle between them (Extended)
triangleArea.rule:
If a triangle has sides a and b with the angle C between them, its area is ½ab sin C. Angle C is at the vertex where sides a and b meet.

The formula comes from the usual rule, area = ½ × base × height. Take a as the base. Then the height is b sin C. The formula works for acute, right-angled and obtuse triangles.

In the exam, check that the angle lies between the two sides you use, and write the answer in square units.
examples: The angle between sides of 6 cm and 8 cm is 30°. Area = ½ × 6 × 8 × sin 30° = 24 × 0.5 = 12 cm².
An equilateral triangle with sides of 10 cm has a 60° angle between any two sides. Area = ½ × 10 × 10 × sin 60° = 25√3 ≈ 43.3 cm².

Check: in a right-angled triangle with legs 6 cm and 8 cm, the angle between the legs is 90°, and sin 90° = 1. The formula gives ½ × 6 × 8 × 1 = 24 cm². This matches the usual ½ × base × height, because the legs are the base and the height.

contrast.en: Do not forget the ½. The product ab sin C gives twice the area of the triangle.
contrast.ru: Не забудь про ½: произведение ab sin C даёт удвоенную площадь треугольника.

circleTheorems.name: Angles and tangents in a circle
circleTheorems.rule:
Circle theorems are rules that link angles and lengths in a circle. They let you find a missing angle without measuring.


The angle at the centre is twice the inscribed angle on the same arc. An inscribed angle has its vertex on the circle.

Inscribed angles on the same arc are equal.

An angle in a semicircle, subtended by a diameter, is 90°.

Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°.

A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

Two tangents drawn from the same point outside a circle have equal lengths.

Check the conditions first. Is the angle at the centre or on the circle? Is a diameter given? Are all four vertices on the circle? Does a line touch the circle at only one point?
examples: The angle at the centre is 80° and subtends arc AB. An inscribed angle on the same arc is half of it: 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.
AB is a diameter of a circle, and C is any other point on the circle. Then angle ACB = 90°, because it is an angle in a semicircle.
ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with ∠A = 70°. Opposite angles add up to 180°, so ∠C = 180° − 70° = 110°.

review.russianTerm: Теоремы об окружностях: углы и касательные

contrast.en: Do not mix up the arcs. An angle stands on the arc between its two arms that does not contain its vertex. If the vertex lies on the minor arc, the angle stands on the major arc, so use 360° minus the minor central angle, then halve it. For a minor central angle of 80°, the angle is (360° − 80°) ÷ 2 = 140°.
contrast.ru: Не путай, на какую дугу опирается угол. Вписанный угол опирается на дугу между его сторонами, которая не содержит вершину. Если вершина лежит на меньшей дуге, угол опирается на большую дугу. Тогда используют 360° минус меньший центральный угол и делят результат на 2. При меньшем центральном угле 80° получится (360° − 80°) ÷ 2 = 140°.

sectors.name: Sectors and arcs
sectors.rule:
A sector is the part of a circle bounded by two radii and an arc.


Arc length: L = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

Sector area: A = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

Perimeter of the sector: P = L + 2r

Here r is the radius (cm), θ is the central angle (°), L is the arc length (cm), A is the sector area (cm²) and P is the perimeter (cm).

Before you calculate, check the data: the radius in cm, the central angle in degrees, and whether you must find the arc length or the area.
examples: Radius 5 cm and central angle 60°. Arc length: L = (60 ÷ 360) × 2π × 5 = 5π/3 ≈ 5.24 cm. Sector area: A = (60 ÷ 360) × π × 5² = 25π/6 ≈ 13.1 cm².
An arc of length 10 cm lies on a circle of radius 4 cm. Find the central angle: θ = (10 ÷ (2π × 4)) × 360° ≈ 143.2°.

contrast.en: Do not mix up the arc and the sector. An arc is part of the circle's boundary, so its length is measured in centimetres (cm). A sector is part of the circle's area, so its area is measured in square centimetres (cm²). Do not put the arc-length formula where the area formula belongs.
contrast.ru: Не путай дугу и сектор. Дуга — часть окружности, её длина измеряется в сантиметрах (см). Сектор — часть круга, его площадь измеряется в квадратных сантиметрах (см²). Не подставляй формулу длины дуги вместо формулы площади.

segments.name: Area of a segment
segments.rule:
A segment (circular segment) is the region between a chord and one of its arcs. The area of the minor segment is the sector area minus the triangle area, where the triangle is formed by the chord and the two radii.

For a minor segment with radius r (cm) and central angle θ (up to 180°):


Sector area: (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

Segment area = sector area − triangle area

Extended: the triangle area is ½r² sin θ, so the segment area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr² − ½r² sin θ.

Before you calculate, check the radius and the central angle. Is the angle up to 180°? If it is, you are finding the minor segment, and the subtraction formula applies.
examples: Radius 6 cm and central angle 90°. Sector area: (90 ÷ 360) × π × 6² = 9π ≈ 28.27 cm². The triangle has two sides of 6 cm with a right angle between them, so its area is ½ × 6 × 6 = 18 cm². Segment area: 9π − 18 ≈ 10.27 cm².
Extended: radius 10 cm and central angle 60°. Sector area: (60 ÷ 360) × π × 10² ≈ 52.36 cm². Triangle area: ½ × 10 × 10 × sin 60° ≈ 43.30 cm². Segment area: 52.36 − 43.30 = 9.06 cm².

contrast.en: Do not give the sector area as the answer for a segment. A sector is bounded by two radii and an arc. A segment is bounded by a chord and an arc, so for a minor segment you must subtract the triangle from the sector.
contrast.ru: Не отвечай площадью сектора, если спрашивают о круговом сегменте. Сектор ограничен двумя радиусами и дугой. Круговой сегмент ограничен хордой и дугой, поэтому для меньшего кругового сегмента из площади сектора вычитают площадь треугольника.

intersectingChords.name: Intersecting chords
intersectingChords.rule:
If two chords AB and CD cross at a point P inside the circle, the product of the two parts of one chord equals the product of the two parts of the other: AP × PB = CP × PD. This is the first case of the intersecting chords theorem.

If the lines AB and CD meet at a point X outside the circle, the same formula holds, using the whole distances from X: AX × BX = CX × DX. This is the second case.

Check first where the chords or lines meet: inside the circle or outside it. This decides which lengths you multiply.
examples: Chords AB and CD cross at P. AP = 6 cm, PB = 4 cm and CP = 3 cm. Find PD: 6 × 4 = 3 × PD, so PD = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 cm.

Two lines meet at X outside the circle. The first line meets the circle at A and B, with AX = 4 cm and BX = 9 cm. The second line meets it at C and D, with CX = 5 cm. Find DX: 4 × 9 = 5 × DX, so DX = 36 ÷ 5 = 7.2 cm. Check: 7.2 cm is longer than 5 cm, so D is the far point, as assumed.

contrast.en: Do not confuse sum and difference. Inside the circle, AB = AP + PB, because P lies between A and B. Outside the circle, X does not lie between A and B, so AB is the difference of the distances from X to A and to B, not their sum. Multiply the distances from X; do not add them.
contrast.ru: Не путай сумму и разность. Внутри окружности AB = AP + PB, потому что P лежит между A и B. Снаружи точка X не лежит между A и B, поэтому AB — разность расстояний от X до A и до B, а не их сумма. Расстояния от X перемножай, а не складывай.

statsProb.title: Statistics & Probability
statsProb.intro: Histograms, box plots, stem-and-leaf plots, grouped data, cumulative frequency, standard deviation (Extended).

representation.name: Data representation — choosing the right chart
representation.rule: Categorical data record labels or classes. Numerical data record counts or measurements; discrete values are separate possibilities, while a continuous variable can take any value in an interval. A bar chart compares categories, a histogram groups numerical values, a line graph shows ordered change, and a scatter plot shows paired numerical observations.
examples: Favourite ice cream flavour → bar chart (categorical).
Heights of students → histogram (continuous data, grouped).
Goals scored per match → bar chart (discrete count).
Temperature vs ice cream sales → scatter graph.

review.englishTerm: Data representation — choosing the right chart

contrast.en: A number used as a label, such as a bus route, need not be quantitative. Histogram intervals have numerical widths; bar-chart categories do not.
contrast.ru: Число-метка, например номер маршрута, не обязательно количественно. Интервалы гистограммы имеют числовую ширину; категории столбчатой диаграммы — нет.

sources.title: OpenStax — 12.3 The Regression Equation — Correlation Coefficient

stemLeaf.name: Stem and leaf diagram
stemLeaf.rule: A stem-and-leaf plot splits each data value at a chosen place value into a stem and a final digit called a leaf. Repeated values keep repeated leaves. Ordered leaves show distribution while preserving the recorded values. A key specifies the scale, for example 2|3=23 or 2|3=2.3.
examples: Back-to-back stem-leaf compares two groups: e.g., boys vs girls heights with shared stems in the middle.

contrast.en: The stem is not always tens. In a back-to-back plot, read each side away from the common stems; include units in the key.
contrast.ru: Стебель не всегда означает десятки. У двусторонней диаграммы каждую сторону читают от общих стеблей; в ключе укажите единицы.

grouped.name: Grouped data — mean, median, mode
grouped.rule: Grouped data record frequencies in nonoverlapping intervals, losing exact individual values. Estimate the mean by Σ(frequency×class midpoint)/Σfrequency. The median splits ordered data into halves; grouping usually identifies its class, with interpolation needed for an estimate. For equal-width classes, the modal class has the greatest frequency.
examples: Intervals [0,10), [10,20), [20,30] have frequencies 4,10,6 and midpoints 5,15,25. Estimated mean=(5·4+15·10+25·6)/20=16.
The modal class is [10,20); both middle observations (10th and 11th) lie there.
A linear grouped-data median estimate uses 10+(10−4)/10·10=16; the exact median is unknown.

contrast.en: Mean, median and mode are distinct measures of centre. For unequal intervals, compare frequency density for the histogram peak; the exact mode is not known from grouped counts.
contrast.ru: Среднее, медиана и мода — разные характеристики центра. При неравных интервалах пик гистограммы определяют по плотности частоты; точная мода по группам неизвестна.

boxPlots.name: Box plots (box-and-whisker)
boxPlots.rule: A box plot marks the median and quartiles Q1,Q3; the box covers the middle half of the data and IQR=Q3−Q1. In a modified box plot, flag values below Q1−1.5·IQR or above Q3+1.5·IQR as potential outliers, and draw whiskers to the most extreme unflagged observations.
examples: Comparing: 'Group A has higher median and larger IQR — more variable than Group B'.

contrast.en: A basic five-number box plot uses min/max whiskers. Do not mix that convention with modified whiskers. A flagged outlier is not automatically an error.
contrast.ru: У простого ящика по пяти числам усы идут до минимума и максимума. Это другое соглашение. Отмеченный выброс не обязательно является ошибкой.

model.en: Here quartiles are medians of the lower and upper halves, excluding the overall median when n is odd. Software can use other conventions.
model.ru: Здесь квартили — медианы нижней и верхней половин; общая медиана при нечётном n исключается. Программы могут использовать другие соглашения.

histograms.name: Histograms (incl. unequal class widths)
histograms.rule: A histogram displays frequencies across numerical intervals. When the vertical axis is frequency density, height=frequency/class width and rectangle area=frequency. Adjacent intervals meet at their boundary; an empty interval can create a gap. Unequal widths require area-based comparison.
examples: Classes: 0–10 (freq 20, width 10, density 2). 10–30 (freq 60, width 20, density 3). 30–60 (freq 30, width 30, density 1).
Total frequency = sum of (density × width). Check: 2·10 + 3·20 + 1·30 = 110.

contrast.en: Bar height alone is not frequency for unequal widths. With equal widths a frequency-height scale is possible, but area is then proportional to frequency.
contrast.ru: При разной ширине сама высота не равна частоте. При равной ширине допустима ось частоты; площадь тогда пропорциональна частоте.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods
sources.section: 1.3.3.14 Histogram — Definition; area normalisation (multiply probability density by sample size for frequency density)

caption.en: These bars have different heights but the same frequency; height is frequency density.
caption.ru: Высоты различаются, но частоты одинаковы; высота задаёт плотность частоты.

cumulativeFreq.name: Cumulative frequency and percentiles
cumulativeFreq.rule: Cumulative frequency is the running total up to a value. For grouped data, plot totals at upper class boundaries and start at the lowest boundary with zero. The graph cannot decrease. Read a pth percentile at cumulative frequency (p/100)N, interpolating between boundaries when necessary.
examples: Linear estimates: median at CF=10 gives 16; Q1 at CF=5 gives 11; Q3 at CF=15 gives 21.67.
90th percentile at CF=18 gives 26.67.

contrast.en: The graph need not be S-shaped. Grouped percentiles are estimates, and flat sections have no observations; do not divide by a zero frequency.
contrast.ru: График не обязан иметь S-образную форму. Процентили по группам — оценки; горизонтальные участки означают отсутствие наблюдений, на нулевую частоту делить нельзя.

model.en: Straight-line interpolation assumes values are spread uniformly inside each interval; the original individual values are unknown.
model.ru: Линейная интерполяция предполагает равномерное распределение внутри интервала; исходные отдельные значения неизвестны.

stdDev.name: Standard deviation (Extended)
stdDev.rule: For a complete finite population x₁,…,x_N with mean μ, variance is σ²=Σ(xᵢ−μ)²/N and standard deviation is σ=√σ². To estimate population variance from a random sample of n>1 observations, use s²=Σ(xᵢ−x̄)²/(n−1). Standard deviation measures spread in the original units.
examples: Compare: data 4.5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5.5 has same mean 5, but σ ≈ 0.289. Much more consistent.

contrast.en: Variance has squared units. The 68% within one standard deviation rule describes a normal distribution, not arbitrary data.
contrast.ru: Дисперсия имеет квадратные единицы. Правило о 68% в пределах одного стандартного отклонения относится к нормальному распределению, а не к любым данным.

pieCharts.name: Pie charts
pieCharts.rule: A pie chart divides a circle into sectors representing nonoverlapping categories of one whole. A category with frequency f out of total N>0 has angle 360°·f/N. All categories together account for 100% and 360°.
examples: Survey of 60 people: 20 walk, 10 cycle, 30 drive. Angles: walk 120°, cycle 60°, drive 180°. Total 360° ✓.
If sector for 'cycle' = 30° in pie of 240 students, count = (30/360)·240 = 20 cyclists.

contrast.en: A category sector shows a proportion, not a raw count without the total. Overlapping categories or multiple-choice responses may not form one whole.
contrast.ru: Сектор показывает долю; без общего числа он не задаёт количество. Пересекающиеся категории или ответы с множественным выбором могут не составлять одно целое.

standardForm.description: Convert a finite nonzero number to a×10ⁿ with 1≤|a|<10. Displayed values are rounded, not a measurement of precision.

contrast.en: 5.4×10⁵=54×10⁴ numerically, but only the first is normalised scientific notation. Standard form has other meanings for polynomials.

quadraticExplorer.title: Quadratic Explorer
quadraticExplorer.description: Explore y=ax²+bx+c. For a≠0 the graph is a parabola; for a=0 it becomes linear or constant. The viewing window can hide roots.

contrast.en: A root is an input value; an intercept is a point. At a repeated root the parabola touches the x-axis without crossing it.
contrast.ru: Корень — значение аргумента, а точка пересечения имеет две координаты. При двукратном корне парабола касается оси x, не пересекая её.

quadraticExplorer.degenerate: a=0: this graph is linear or constant; it has no quadratic vertex.
quadraticExplorer.alt: Graph of y={{a}}x²+{{b}}x+{{c}}. Read the roots and vertex in the adjacent text; the visible x-range is −10 to 10.

sequenceGenerator.title: Sequence Generator
sequenceGenerator.description: Generate terms indexed by n=1,2,…: add d for arithmetic sequences or multiply by r for geometric ones. Dots mark discrete terms.

review.englishTerm: Geometric sequences and the nth term
review.russianTerm: Геометрическая прогрессия и формула n-го члена

contrast.en: Arithmetic sequences add a fixed difference; geometric sequences multiply by a fixed ratio. For a>0, r>1 gives growth and 0<r<1 gives decay; negative r alternates signs.
contrast.ru: Арифметическая прогрессия прибавляет разность, геометрическая — умножает на знаменатель. При a>0 и r>1 получается рост, при 0<r<1 — убывание; отрицательное r чередует знаки.

sequenceGenerator.alt: Discrete sequence dots at positive integer indices. The full list of terms is printed above.

sectorSegment.title: Sector & Segment Calculator
sectorSegment.description: Blue shows the sector bounded by radii; orange shows the segment bounded by chord and arc. Angles above 180° select the major arc and major segment.

contrast.en: Sector and segment share an arc but have different straight boundaries. The positive triangle-subtraction picture applies to minor segments.
contrast.ru: У сектора и сегмента может быть общая дуга, но разные прямолинейные границы. Вычитание положительной площади треугольника относится к меньшему сегменту.

model.ru: Калькулятор допускает и большую дугу: ½r²(θ−sin θ), где θ в радианах, использует знак синуса при π<θ<2π.

boxPlot.title: Box Plot Builder
boxPlot.description: Build a modified box plot. Quartiles are medians of the two halves, excluding an odd middle value. Whiskers end at the most extreme values within the 1.5·IQR fences.

contrast.en: A basic five-number box plot uses min/max whiskers. Do not mix that convention with modified whiskers. A flagged outlier is not automatically an error.
contrast.ru: У простого ящика по пяти числам усы идут до минимума и максимума. Это другое соглашение. Отмеченный выброс не обязательно является ошибкой.

model.en: Here quartiles are medians of the lower and upper halves, excluding the overall median when n is odd. Software can use other conventions.
model.ru: Здесь квартили — медианы нижней и верхней половин; общая медиана при нечётном n исключается. Программы могут использовать другие соглашения.

boxPlot.input: Dataset: separate numbers with spaces, commas or semicolons; use a decimal point.
boxPlot.alt: Box plot: Q1 {{q1}}, median {{median}}, Q3 {{q3}}; whiskers at {{lower}} and {{upper}}. Outliers are separate dots.

surdSimplifier.title: Surd Simplifier
surdSimplifier.description: Simplify √n for integers 1≤n≤1000. A perfect-square input produces a rational result; not every radical is a surd.

contrast.en: A radical is the root notation; a surd has an irrational value. √9=3 is a radical expression but not a surd. π is irrational but is not a surd.
contrast.ru: Радикал — знак корня; surd имеет иррациональное значение. √9=3 записано с радикалом, но это не surd. Число π иррационально, но не является surd.

transformations.title: Function Transformations
transformations.description: Transform a graph by y=a·f(x−h)+k. Sine uses radians; reciprocal curves have gaps at excluded inputs. The case a=0 keeps the original domain.

contrast.en: f(2x) halves horizontal distances: its horizontal scale factor is 1/2. Scaling and translation generally depend on their order.

contrast.en: An expression is evaluated or transformed; an equation is solved. No real roots does not mean no complex roots.
contrast.ru: Выражение вычисляют или преобразуют; уравнение решают. Отсутствие действительных корней не означает отсутствия комплексных.

rightTriangle.description: Change the positive legs of a right triangle. θ is at the left vertex: the horizontal leg is adjacent and the vertical leg opposite.

contrast.en: sin⁻¹ denotes arcsin on a calculator, not 1/sin. This triangle definition uses 0°<θ<90°; unit-circle definitions extend the functions.

numberSetsVenn.title: Number Sets — Venn
numberSetsVenn.description: Classify exact integer/fraction/finite-decimal inputs, π, e, and integer multiples of √n (0≤n≤1,000,000). Here ℕ starts at 1. Other expressions are unsupported.
numberSetsVenn.irrational: Irrational: belongs to ℝ and not ℚ (among the four sets shown).
numberSetsVenn.properFraction: A non-integer rational number: belongs to ℚ and ℝ.
numberSetsVenn.positiveWhole: A positive whole number — belongs to all four sets.
numberSetsVenn.integer: An integer (including 0 or negative) — ℤ, ℚ, ℝ.
numberSetsVenn.finiteDecimal: A finite decimal — rational (ℚ) and real (ℝ).

contrast.en: An element and a subset are different: 2∈ℕ but {2}⊆ℕ. Some books include 0 in ℕ; state the convention.
contrast.ru: Элемент и подмножество различаются: 2∈ℕ, но {2}⊆ℕ. В некоторых учебниках 0 включают в ℕ; соглашение нужно указывать.

bearingsCompass.description: A flat-map bearing is measured clockwise from north at the origin. East offset=d sin θ; north offset=d cos θ.

contrast.en: The bearing of B from A starts at A. The reverse bearing is (θ+180°) modulo 360°, assuming parallel north directions.
contrast.ru: Азимут B из A отсчитывают в A. Обратный азимут равен (θ+180°) по модулю 360° при параллельных направлениях севера.

cumulativeFreq.title: Cumulative Frequency Curve

contrast.en: The graph need not be S-shaped. Grouped percentiles are estimates, and flat sections have no observations; do not divide by a zero frequency.
contrast.ru: График не обязан иметь S-образную форму. Процентили по группам — оценки; горизонтальные участки означают отсутствие наблюдений, на нулевую частоту делить нельзя.

model.en: Straight-line interpolation assumes values are spread uniformly inside each interval; the original individual values are unknown.

circleTheorems.title: Circle Theorems Playground
circleTheorems.description: Explore valid Euclidean circle constructions: the inscribed-angle, semicircle, cyclic-quadrilateral and intersecting-chord theorems.
circleTheorems.ruleCentre: The central angle subtending the intercepted arc is twice the inscribed angle; C is not on that arc.
circleTheorems.ruleSemicircle: For diameter AB and C on the circle distinct from A,B, ∠ACB=90°.
circleTheorems.ruleCyclic: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°.
circleTheorems.ruleChords: When two chords intersect, the products of their segments are equal: AP × PB = CP × PD.

contrast.en: The intercepted arc excludes the inscribed angle’s vertex. For the tangent–chord theorem, choose the angle in the alternate segment; do not just match any angle.
contrast.ru: Перехваченная дуга не содержит вершину вписанного угла. В теореме об угле между касательной и хордой выбирайте вписанный угол в противоположном сегменте.
